items.title: /forgot-password and /resend-verification have no rate limit — mailbomb / token-clobber
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/auth.rs:1461 — check_rate_limit is only invoked on /login (line 555). /forgot-password and /resend-verification generate + persist a token and enqueue an email on every request with NO per-email, per-IP, or global throttle. Attacker who knows a target email can mailbomb their inbox (phishing amplification) and burn the org's email-service quota. The intentional generic response also means there's no feedback loop to detect abuse. And because every hit invalidates prior tokens, a bystander who knows the email can break an in-flight password reset.

items.title: SECURITY: Alexa voice webhook accepts forged requests — verify_alexa_signature never checks the signature
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:750 — verify_alexa_signature() binds the Signature header to `_signature` and never uses it. It validates only the SignatureCertChainUrl format (validate_alexa_cert_url) and the body timestamp (validate_alexa_timestamp), then returns Ok(()). The in-code comment admits steps 3 & 4 (fetch cert chain, verify signature with the cert public key) are unimplemented.

Reachable and stateful: voice_webhook_router() is mounted at lib.rs:340 under /api/v1/webhooks/voice, and alexa_webhook (voice_webhooks.rs:95) takes an `RlsConnection` — so a forged request reaches tenant data.

Exploit shape: POST /api/v1/webhooks/voice/alexa with SignatureCertChainUrl=https://s3.amazonaws.com/echo.api/x, any non-empty Signature header, and a body timestamp inside the 150s window is accepted as an authentic Alexa delivery.
Secondary: the /verify helper endpoint (voice_webhooks.rs:698) reports alexa signatures as `valid: !request.signature.is_empty()` — a self-described 'simplified check for demo'.

Fix direction: mirror the repo's existing hardened webhook convention (routes/portal_webhooks.rs::verify_timestamped_portal_webhook, routes/layout/webhook.rs::sign_timestamped_payload) or add real x509 chain validation via x509-parser; until then the route should fail closed.

evidence: .github/workflows/api-validation.yml triggers only on `docs/api/**` (push and pull_request). The `generate-sdks` drift gate that compares the committed frontend/packages/api-client/src/generated tree against a fresh openapi-ts run was added 2026-07-22 in PR #2444 (7e982cf91).
docs/api/** has not changed on dev since 902110d (2026-07-19), so the gate has NEVER executed on dev with the gate present — the last green dev run predates it.

Both api-validation runs since the gate landed failed: 2026-07-23 (auto-impl/refactor-churn-hotspot-ppt-dashboard-md-1efc81ca) and 2026-07-28 (auto-impl/refactor-churn-hotspot-repo-map-md-2026-5bfbe482, run 30399201262). The failure is real committed drift — the artifact downloaded and verified its digest cleanly; the regenerated client differs from the committed one by a large export-type set.
Consequence 1: dev ships an @ppt/api-client that does not match docs/api/typespec, and no scheduled or dev-push run can catch it.

Consequence 2: unrelated docs-only PRs inherit a red required check they did not cause — currently blocking PR #2482 (a docs/repo-map.md-only change). A force-push that re-bases such a branch widens the push-event path comparison enough to trip the docs/api/** filter.

Fix direction: (a) regenerate and commit the client in its own PR to clear the standing drift, and (b) widen the trigger so the gate actually guards — add frontend/packages/api-client/** to the paths, or run generate-sdks on every push to dev (it needs the validate job's openapi-spec artifact, so keep the job dependency).
Note the workflow's own comment: @ppt/reality-api-client is explicitly NOT gated (older generator template set) — that carve-out compounds the blind spot.

items.title: mobile: useOfflineSupport — transient (5xx/network) queued actions are permanently DROPPED after 3 retries with only console.error — silent loss of offline-created content

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:399-401 — carriedForward = queue.filter(a => !succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)); anything in terminalFailureIds is excluded from `merged` and thus deleted from QUEUE_KEY on the subsequent AsyncStorage.setItem. frontend/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:81-83,337 — the sync-toast's only recovery is onRetry={handleRetrySync} which just calls processQueue() again. Because the terminally-dropped action is no longer in the queue, tapping Retry cannot recover it. For queued fault reports/meter readings/votes/acknowledgements made while offline this is silent data loss after transient server unavailability.
Fix: treat only isPermanent (4xx) as terminal; give transient failures a larger bounded budget or move them to a dead-letter store surfaced in the UI rather than deleting them.

routes/lazyRoutes.tsx defines ~90 `lazy(() => import(...))` page chunks. A rejected dynamic import is NOT caught by Suspense — it propagates as a thrown error. After a redeploy, a user holding a stale index.html requests an old hashed chunk that no longer exists on the CDN (404) — a routine production event for a Vite hashed-chunk SPA. components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:99 handleRetry only resets `hasError` and re-renders — for a failed lazy() import the browser has permanently cached the rejected module promise, so 'Try Again' re-throws immediately; only 'Reload Page' (window.location.reload, :182) recovers.

Fix: wrap `<Suspense><AppRoutes/></Suspense>` in App.tsx:229 with a route-scoped `<ErrorBoundary>` (component supports a custom `fallback`) so failures are contained to the `<main>` outlet, keeping AppNavigation/shell mounted. items.title: mobile-rn: the cold-start initialize() effect reads the stored access token (SecureSto...
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:85-95 — the cold-start `initialize()` effect reads the stored access token (`SecureStore.getItemAsync(ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY)`) and, whenever both `accessToken` and `userJson` are present, unconditionally sets `{ isLoading:false, isAuthenticated:true, user, accessToken }`. It never decodes/checks the token's `exp` claim and never calls the existing `refreshToken()`. Because access tokens are short-lived (refresh tokens are the long-lived credential — see REFRESH_TOKEN_KEY / the /auth/refresh flow at :209-231), any app cold-start that happens after the stored access token's TTL has elapsed restores the user into an `isAuthenticated:true` state holding an already-expired bearer token.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:296-312 — `authenticateWithBiometric` has the identical gap on the unlock path: after `LocalAuthentication.authenticateAsync` succeeds it reads the stored `accessToken`/`userJson` and sets `isAuthenticated:true` with that token, with an explicit comment (":296") that it deliberately does NOT refetch/reset (issue #2399) — but it also performs no `exp` validation and no proactive `refreshToken()`, so a biometric unlock after the access token expired lands the user authenticated-but-with-an-expired-token.

This compounds the already-filed `code-review-mobile-rn-useapi-no-refresh-retry` (the API layer does not transparently refresh + retry on 401): with no proactive refresh at restore/unlock AND no reactive refresh-retry in useApi, the first request after an expired restore 401s and the user is stuck in a broken 'logged in but everything fails' state until a manual logout/login. `refreshToken()` already exists in this same context (:209) and is simply never invoked on the two restore paths. Fix: on `initialize()` and on successful biometric unlock, decode the access token's `exp` (utils/jwt.ts already ships a guarded `decodeJwtPayload`) and, if expired/near-expiry, `await refreshToken()` before setting `isAuthenticated:true` (fall back to the login screen if refresh fails).

items.title: ppt-web-core: the client heartbeat sends an APPLICATION-level ping frame {type:'ping', pa...
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:688-709 — the client heartbeat sends an APPLICATION-level ping frame `{type:'ping', payload:null, timestamp}` via send() every heartbeatInterval (default 30000ms, :288), sets `awaitingPong = true`, and arms a pongTimeout (default 10000ms, :289). The ONLY thing that clears awaitingPong is receiving a text frame whose `data.type === 'pong'` (handleMessage :529-532 -> handlePong :711-718). If no such frame arrives within 10s, `this.socket?.close(4000, 'Pong timeout')` fires (:705), producing a non-clean close -> onclose (:495-510) -> scheduleReconnect().

The api-server notification WS handler NEVER sends an application-level `{type:'pong'}`. Verified in backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/ws_notifications.rs: the server only emits `Message::Text` carrying the `{event, payload}` WsEvent envelope (:219-230) for notifications, and uses PROTOCOL-level `Message::Ping(vec![])` for its own liveness probe (:242). Its inbound arm (:257-260) explicitly treats every client frame (Text/Binary/Ping/Pong) as a heartbeat and returns without replying — see the module header comment (:27, 'Client -> server: any message is treated as a heartbeat (pong)'). No code path serialises the string 'pong' back to the client.

Consequence: on every connection the client opens (onopen -> startHeartbeat :488-493), 30s later it sends `{type:'ping'}`, the server swallows it, awaitingPong stays true, and at ~40s the client force-closes with code 4000 and reconnects. onclose->stopHeartbeat->scheduleReconnect->connect->onopen->startHeartbeat repeats the cycle indefinitely. parseServerMessage (:59-76) maps real notification events onto `type = <event name>`, never 'pong', so an incoming notification never clears awaitingPong either. The realtime notification channel therefore drops and reconnects roughly every 40s for the entire authenticated session.

Reachability confirmed in production: App.tsx:94-101 mounts <WebSocketProvider> around the whole authenticated app with NO heartbeatInterval/pongTimeout override, so the 30s/10s defaults apply; WebSocketContext.tsx:250-251 calls service.connect() whenever auth.isAuthenticated && accessToken. Impact: constant socket churn, missed pushes during each reconnect gap, redundant server WS-session setup/teardown, and spurious onDisconnected/onReconnected callback firing every ~40s. Fix: the client-side app-level ping is both wrong (server never answers it) and redundant (the server already pings and the browser auto-pongs at the protocol level, invisible to JS). Remove the sendPing/pongTimeout logic and rely on the server's Message::Ping + browser auto-pong for liveness; OR have the server echo an application `{type:'pong'}` on receipt of `{type:'ping'}` so the contract matches. Distinct from the prior ws-token-rotation-stale and ws-ungated-console findings.

items.title: ppt-web-core: once reconnectAttempts reaches maxReconnectAttempts (default 10, :290) sche...
evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/websocket.ts:600-612 — once reconnectAttempts reaches maxReconnectAttempts (default 10, :290) scheduleReconnect() sets `shouldReconnect = false`, emits `connection:max-retries-exceeded`, and sets an error state. From that point NOTHING in the client re-arms reconnection: onclose only reconnects when shouldReconnect is true (:507), and reconnectAttempts is never reset by connect() or disconnect() — only a successful onopen resets it (:489). The public resetReconnectAttempts() (:479-481) is dead code (no caller in the segment).

The default backoff sum (min 1000ms doubling, capped at 30000ms, over 10 attempts) is only ~3 minutes, so any real outage longer than that — laptop sleep, tunnel/VPN drop, backend redeploy window, mobile network gap — permanently kills the notification socket for the rest of the session.

There is no auto-resume wiring. contexts/WebSocketContext.tsx only calls service.connect() on an auth change (:246-256); it never subscribes to `connection:max-retries-exceeded` and is not connected to hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts (which already detects browser online/offline transitions, useNetworkStatus.ts:96-121). So when connectivity returns, the socket stays dead until the user logs out/in or reloads the page — user silently stops receiving realtime pushes with no indication and no recovery path.

Fix: on the browser `online` event (or via useNetworkStatusEffect) call service.connect() to resume, and have connect() reset reconnectAttempts (or call resetReconnectAttempts()) so a fresh attempt budget is granted; optionally surface the `connection:max-retries-exceeded` state in WebSocketContext so the UI can offer a manual reconnect. Net-new — no prior ppt-web-core finding covered the reconnect give-up / resume lifecycle.

items.title: Quiet-hours drain marks held push released even when delivery failed (sent=0) — held notification permanently lost on transient failure
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/quiet_hours_drain.rs:135-140 captures `let sent = self.pipeline.deliver_held(&held).await;` but NEVER checks `sent`; it calls mark_notification_released(held.id) unconditionally and only retries (continue) when the DB mark itself errors. items.title: Reports CSV export writes user-authored vote titles unescaped — spreadsheet formula injection (bypasses the repo's own sanitize_csv_cell)

items.title: SECURITY: public access_protected_share endpoint verifies share password with no rate-limit / lockout — brute-force at request speed
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/shares.rs:574 access_protected_share -- public, unauthenticated endpoint (mounted via shares::public_router at POST /api/v1/documents/shared/{token}/access, lib.rs:165 merge) verifies a caller-supplied share password (verify_share_password_for_share at ~L617) with NO brute-force protection: no failed-attempt counter, no per-token/per-IP lockout, no throttle. grep for rate.?limit|throttle|attempt|lockout across routes/documents/ returns 0 hits.

The only rate limiter in api-server is a per-TENANT set (state.tenant_rate_limiters: TenantRateLimiterSet, applied through host_tenant_middleware keyed on org context). The share handler comment explicitly states 'This public endpoint has no caller org context', so the per-tenant limiter cannot key these unauthenticated requests -> the password endpoint is effectively unthrottled. An attacker holding a share token can brute-force the share password at request speed.

The parallel signer endpoint (routes/signatures::public_sign_router) and other public flows should be checked for the same gap. Fix: add per-token (and/or per-IP) attempt throttling + exponential backoff/lockout on access_protected_share before verify, or gate the public_router behind a dedicated unauthenticated-rate-limit layer.

items.title: share access log records proxy IP without CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For unwind — misattributes source
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/shares.rs:437 & :574 -- both public share handlers derive the audit ip_address from axum ConnectInfo<SocketAddr> (let ip_address = addr.ip().to_string()) and persist it via log_share_access_for_share(LogShareAccess{ ip_address, .. }).

ConnectInfo is the DIRECT TCP peer. In this deployment the api-server sits behind a reverse proxy / load balancer (per repo architecture: nginx + *<internal-dev-host-redacted>), so addr.ip() is the proxy's address for every request -- the share-access audit log records the proxy IP, not the real client, for all public document-share accesses.

The code comments call this write 'important for audit trail', but the recorded IP is not attacker-attributable and is identical across all clients, undermining the audit value and defeating any future IP-based abuse detection. Fix: resolve the client IP from a validated forwarded-for chain (trusted-proxy-aware, e.g. axum-client-ip / a checked X-Forwarded-For) instead of the raw socket peer.

items.title: payment matcher never surfaces multiple suggestions — early-return on first match hides equally-good candidates
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:124-176 (AccountingService::run_payment_matcher) — the once-only guard `if line.match_state != "unmatched" && line.match_state != "suggested" { continue; }` is at the TOP of the outer `for line in lines` loop (L125-127), evaluated once per line BEFORE the inner `for invoice in &open_invoices` loop (L129). Inside the inner loop the code, on every invoice whose confidence >= 0.5, upserts a PaymentMatch (L162 upsert_payment_match_rls) AND sets the line to "suggested" (L167 update_bank_statement_line_match_state_rls) but does NOT `break`. So a single bank-statement line is matched against EVERY qualifying open invoice, not just the first — the state update that marks the line as "suggested" never short-circuits the remaining invoices.

The line's in-memory `line.match_state` is a move-captured value from the pre-loop snapshot (repo.list_bank_statement_lines_rls at L104) and is never mutated after the DB write, and `remaining_amount = invoice.total_amount - invoice.paid_amount` (L141) is likewise read from the pre-loop `list_invoices_rls` snapshot and never decremented as suggestions accumulate. Consequence: one payment can be suggested as (partially/fully) paying N different invoices, and one invoice can absorb N different lines, because neither side's remaining balance is reduced within the run. When several open invoices share a variable symbol (0.8) the same line is auto-suggested against all of them.

The write of `match_state = "suggested"` after the first hit signals a 1:1 intent (one suggested match per line), which the un-broken inner loop contradicts — over-generating PaymentMatch rows in the accounting reconciliation flow that a human then has to reject. Fix options: `break` out of the inner loop after the first suggestion (keep best-scoring by tracking max-confidence invoice and suggesting only that), and/or decrement a mutable running `remaining` per invoice and skip invoices already fully covered by prior suggestions.

items.title: payment matcher uses a single VS-only threshold — ignores IBAN / amount tie-breakers documented in spec
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:132-150 — a Variable-Symbol match alone adds 0.8 (L136) which already clears the 0.5 auto-suggest threshold (L150), while the amount signal contributes at most 0.15 (exact match, L143) or 0.05 (L145) and is NEVER required. A bank line that merely shares a variable symbol with an invoice is therefore suggested regardless of amount — e.g. a small partial/erroneous payment suggested against a large invoice, or a payment suggested against an invoice with a totally different remaining balance.

The matcher is also explicitly incomplete: `// TODO: Date proximity, IBAN match` (L148). Two of the four intended corroboration signals are unimplemented, so the confidence score currently rests almost entirely on the VS field, which is user-supplied on the bank side and not guaranteed unique per invoice.

Suggested hardening: require a minimum amount corroboration before crossing the auto-suggest threshold (e.g. VS-only should stay below 0.5, or the amount branch weight should be raised so an amount mismatch can veto a VS-only match), and/or gate auto-suggestion on `line.amount <= remaining_amount` so a payment is never suggested against an invoice it cannot plausibly settle.

items.title: NFC emergencyRevokeAll leaves local credentials usable offline when the revoke API call fails
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts:223-227 — emergencyRevokeAll() awaits apiRequest('/api/v1/access/credentials/revoke-all') FIRST, then clears this.credentials and secure-store. If the network call throws (device offline — the exact 'lost phone' scenario this method serves), the exception propagates before the local clear runs, so the encrypted credential blob stays in SecureStore.

NFC access (NFCAccessController.validateAccess / handleTap) works fully offline against the cached credential list, so a failed revoke means the lost/stolen device retains working building-access credentials until validUntil expiry.
Fix: clear local credentials regardless of the API outcome (clear-first or in a finally block), and surface the sync failure to the caller so the server-side revoke can be retried.

items.title: NFC credentials stored as one SecureStore value can exceed the ~2KB cap, silently dropping fetched credentials
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts:20-24,292-294 — storeCredentials() writes JSON.stringify(this.credentials) into a single SecureStore slot; the file's own comment acknowledges SecureStore's ~2KB per-value cap yet claims one slot is 'plenty for tens of entries'.

Each NFCCredential (types.ts:10-35) carries encryptedData (NFC HCE payload), a buildingName, and an accessPoints[] array (each with id/name/type/zone/floor/timeRestrictions) — a handful of credentials easily exceeds 2KB, and expo-secure-store rejects/warns on oversized values on Android.

fetchCredentials() (lines 60-75) awaits storeCredentials() inside its try block, so a size-related throw is swallowed and it returns the stale cached list — freshly fetched/refreshed credentials are silently lost; refreshCredential()/updateCredentialUsage() are unguarded and would reject.

Fix: chunk credentials across multiple SecureStore keys (or store a manifest + per-credential slots), or store the bulk list in encrypted AsyncStorage with only secrets in SecureStore; do not assume the whole array fits one 2KB slot.

items.title: NFC getAccessLog JSON.parse is unguarded, so a corrupted log blob rejects handleTap after access was already granted
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts:160-163 — getAccessLog() does `JSON.parse(stored)` with no try/catch, unlike the carefully corruption-guarded loadStoredCredentials() (lines 262-290) which discards a bad blob.

logAccessAttempt() (142-147) awaits getAccessLog(); NFCAccessController.handleTap() (nfc/NFCAccessController.ts:211-217) awaits logAccessAttempt() with no try/catch, so a corrupted @ppt/access_log blob throws and rejects handleTap — the already-computed granted AccessAttemptResult is never returned and the UI shows an error for a door that actually opened.
Fix: wrap the getAccessLog parse in try/catch (discard + reset on failure), mirroring the credential-load hardening.

items.title: reality-server saved-search alert loop swallows the watermark-advance error (let _ =), re-enqueuing duplicate alerts on the next due run
evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/saved_search_alerts.rs:237-240 — the watermark-advancing `repo.mark_saved_search_matched(&mut *conn, search.id, ids.len() as i64)` call is `let _ =`-discarded, so an UPDATE error is silently ignored and last_matched_at is not advanced.

The enqueue at :216-231 already committed (`enqueue_search_alert(...)` returned Ok and `queued += 1`), so when the subsequent mark fails the alert rows are already queued but the watermark still points at the old `since`. On the next due poll `find_new_match_listing_ids(&query, Some(since), ...)` at :197-205 re-derives the identical result set and `enqueue_search_alert` fires again — the same new listings are delivered to the user a second (and further) time.

Contrast with the sibling backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/favorite_alerts.rs:118,160-164 which deliberately wraps enqueue + watermark-advance in a single `REPEATABLE READ` transaction to keep the two writes atomic (documented against #1999). saved_search_alerts runs them as two separate autocommitted statements with the advance's Result swallowed, giving no atomicity and no failure signal. Fix: propagate/log the mark error and either advance the watermark in the same transaction as the enqueue or skip the enqueue-count so a failed advance doesn't double-notify.

items.title: SSO introspect_pm_token caches active=false on PM 5xx — 60s spurious session denials during PM introspection outages
evidence: routes/sso.rs:729-786 introspect_pm_token caches in state.token_cache (TokenValidationCache, 60s TTL, state.rs:947); on the FAILURE branch at :759-766 when the PM endpoint returns non-success HTTP, it calls `state.token_cache.set(token, false, None, None)` — caches active=false for a token whose real status is UNKNOWN

Per RFC 7662 a genuinely inactive token is HTTP 200 with `{active: false}` (handled at :770-784); a 4xx/5xx means client-config or upstream error (PM API down/redeploy, 502/503, bad credentials) — NOT authoritative evidence the user's token is inactive. Caching false on !is_success() treats an upstream outage as an authoritative negative

Cache-hit path (:735-745) returns `Ok(TokenIntrospectionResponse { active: cached.active, .. })` for any non-expired entry with NO error signal (state.rs:656-673 returns any entry while `Instant::now() < cached.expires_at`), so during a PM blip the first request 5xx-fails + writes active=false; every subsequent request with that SAME valid token for up to 60s hits the poisoned cache and is denied. Common because a page fires several bearer-token calls

Fails CLOSED (denies rather than grants), so availability defect not security bypass — scored +2 medium. Fix (routes/sso.rs only): populate cache ONLY from a successfully-parsed 200 body (cache both active=true and PM's genuine active=false); on any transport/non-2xx error return Err WITHOUT calling token_cache.set. Backend Rust only, landable in cloud. IG3: unit test that a 503 introspection leaves token_cache empty and a following 200 re-validates active=true

items.title: SSO exchange/userinfo/introspect create a fresh reqwest::Client per request with no timeout — no pooling, hang risk
evidence: All three PM-facing SSO helpers construct a brand-new HTTP client per request via `reqwest::Client::new()`: exchange_pm_token (routes/sso.rs:687), get_user_info (:711), and introspect_pm_token (:748) — fresh connection pool + TLS setup on every authenticated portal request

`reqwest::Client::new()` applies NO request timeout. A hung/slow PM endpoint (the very outage scenario in the paired negcache-poison finding) can stall these helpers indefinitely, holding the portal request open. Contrast state.rs:756-762 where PmApiClient::new builds its client with `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds))` — the timeout discipline exists but is not applied here

Fix: build a shared `reqwest::Client` once with explicit `.timeout(...)` mirroring PmApiClient — store on AppState alongside existing PmApiClient or pass the already-pooled client — and reuse across exchange_pm_token / get_user_info / introspect_pm_token. Backend Rust only, landable in cloud. IG3: test that the SSO helpers use a client with a configured timeout, or construction-site assertion that no bare `Client::new()` remains in sso.rs

items.title: Reality Portal length validators measure bytes but errors say characters — over-rejects sk/cs/de accented input
evidence: Every user-facing length validation on the public Reality Portal write paths measures BYTES (str::len()) but constants and 400 error messages are all phrased in CHARACTERS — Slovak/Czech/German accented chars are 2 bytes/char and emoji are 4 bytes, so a submission well under the advertised character cap is rejected once its UTF-8 byte length crosses the limit (a ~2500-char Slovak message already trips a 5000-char cap)

inquiries.rs:43-55 validate_inquiry_lengths — name.len() > 200, email.len() > 320, phone > 32, message.len() > 5000 with 'max 5000 characters' error. inquiries.rs:425-464 request_viewing repeats the same inline. inquiries.rs:786-789 respond_to_inquiry uses `if req.message.len() > 5000` with 'less than 5000 characters' AND a magic 5000 instead of MAX_INQUIRY_MESSAGE_LEN

articles.rs:456-461 create_comment — data.body.len() > MAX_COMMENT_BODY_LEN error 'at most {} characters'. agent_reviews.rs:212-215 create_review — body.len() > MAX_REVIEW_BODY_LEN error 'at most {} characters'. reports.rs:~200 submit_report — description.len() > MAX_REPORT_DESCRIPTION_LEN error 'at most {} characters'

Fix: measure grapheme-ish length consistently with the messaging — replace .len() with .chars().count() on these free-text fields and route respond_to_inquiry through MAX_INQUIRY_MESSAGE_LEN. Byte caps may still be wanted as an explicit DoS backstop but should be a separate, explicitly-byte-worded guard. Backend Rust, multi-file (4 route files). Landable in cloud. IG3: unit test asserting N accented chars (byte length ~2N) at N <= limit is accepted

items.title: submit_report reporter_email/reporter_phone bound into INSERT with no length or format validation
evidence: submit_report (routes/reports.rs, POST /api/v1/reports, UC-23) is an optionally-authenticated/anonymous-allowed endpoint (OptionalRequestPrincipal). It validates description (non-empty + MAX_REPORT_DESCRIPTION_LEN) and attachments (count cap + per-URL validate_image_or_link_url), but reporter_email and reporter_phone (SubmitReportRequest reports.rs:91-92) are bound straight into the INSERT at :279-280 with NO length and NO format validation

Impact: unbounded unauthenticated free-text per allowed report — table/column bloat, junk contact data surfaced to moderators, and (if the DB column has a length constraint) a raw DB error mapped to generic 500 via db_error() instead of a clean 400 — same failure mode the listings pagination clamp (#953) prevented

Fix: apply the existing inquiry caps/validators to reporter_email/reporter_phone before the INSERT (reject when reporter_email > MAX_INQUIRY_EMAIL_LEN or reporter_phone > MAX_INQUIRY_PHONE_LEN, optionally reuse validate_contact), return 400 with a generic message (do NOT echo offending value — same reflected-XSS caution the file already documents for attachment URLs). Backend Rust only, single-file, landable in cloud. IG3: integration test that an over-length reporter_email yields 400

items.title: api-server push_fanout: FCM HTTP v1 uses a static FCM_OAUTH_TOKEN loaded once at startup — Google's ~1h token TTL breaks Android push after first hour
evidence: push_fanout.rs:233 `oauth_token: std::env::var("FCM_OAUTH_TOKEN").ok()` loaded once at FcmConfig::from_env(); reused verbatim as bearer at :330-341 (`.bearer_auth(&bearer)`). FCM HTTP v1 access tokens are OAuth2, ~3600s TTL — no refresh path from a service-account key anywhere in the module.

Wired path: PushFanoutWorker.deliver_job -> CombinedPushAdapter.send -> FcmHttpAdapter.send_fcm_v1. Not dev-gated. Inline comment at :324-329 acknowledges the shortcut ('In production this would come from a service-account key file via google-cloud-auth').
Impact: Android push channel silently 401s ~1h post-boot until process restart. In-app notifications remain the mandatory record, so no data loss, but a shipped delivery channel silently degrades.

Routine 2026-09-01 verified via grep: `oauth_token: std::env::var("FCM_OAUTH_TOKEN")` at :233, `let bearer = self.fcm_config.oauth_token.clone()` at :330, `.bearer_auth(&bearer)` at :341 — code path confirmed live.

resolved: PR #2914 merged 2026-09-01 — fix(api-server): auto-refresh FCM HTTP v1 OAuth2 access token. Added FcmTokenProvider with service-account variant that mints RS256 JWT and refreshes before expiry; static FCM_OAUTH_TOKEN retained only as documented legacy fallback (lines 242/553 explicitly comment the deprecation).

items.title: api-server push_fanout: ApnsHttpAdapter mints a fresh ES256 provider-authentication JWT on EVERY send (deliver_job:1383 -> :902) — no cache; Apple documents JWT reuse for up to 60min
evidence: push_fanout.rs:901-909 `ApnsHttpAdapter::deliver` calls `mint_apns_jwt(&self.apns_config)` (fn at :699-733) for every notification; deliver_job (:1383) processes one Notification per queue job. No token cache.

APNs guidance is to reuse the provider JWT for its lifetime (up to 1h) — per-send minting wastes CPU on the delivery hot path and Apple rate-limits token minting; sustained high-volume send bursts risk `TooManyProviderTokenUpdates`.

Fix shape: hold the minted JWT + iat inside ApnsHttpAdapter (Mutex<Option<(String, DateTime<Utc>)>>), refresh only when older than ~50min; keeps mint_apns_jwt as-is for a single unit-testable seam. Aligns with the pooled-SSO-client pattern PR #2897 landed for reality-server.

items.title: api-server push_fanout: FCM legacy fallback (`https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send`) is Google-decommissioned dead code — send_fcm_legacy can never deliver in production
evidence: push_fanout.rs:330-336 falls back to `send_fcm_legacy` (fn at :395-426) when no FCM_OAUTH_TOKEN is configured; `send_fcm_legacy` POSTs to `{base_url}/fcm/send` (default base_url `https://fcm.googleapis.com`, :247) with `Authorization: key={FCM_SERVER_KEY}`.
Google decommissioned the legacy HTTP API on 2024-06-20 — `POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send` returns 404/401 for all callers. The fallback is unreachable except for a mock base_url.

Fix shape: delete send_fcm_legacy + the FCM_SERVER_KEY branch of send_fcm_v1, and tighten the config so v1 is required (return a startup error when FCM_PROJECT_ID is set without OAuth wiring). Tied to the fcm-v1-static-oauth-token item — both live in the same file and share test scaffolding.

items.title: api-server compliance.rs get_user_audit_logs: `total = log_responses.len()` returns the page size, not the true user-audit-log count — UI paginator hides pages 2..N on a compliance surface
evidence: get_user_audit_logs (routes/compliance.rs:257-298, GET /api/v1/compliance/audit-logs/user/{user_id}) computes `let total = log_responses.len() as i64;` (:291). The handler fetches ONE page via `get_user_logs(user_id, limit.unwrap_or(100), offset.unwrap_or(0))` (:264-270) and never issues a count query. The response's `total` field ends up equal to the page size (100 on default), so any UI paginator dividing total by limit sees `1 page` and hides pages 2..N.

Distinct from unbounded-pagination-limit (clamp of `limit`, done in #2911) and from superadmin-exact-match. Sibling handler get_audit_logs (:124-179) does it correctly, calling state.audit_log_repo.count(query) for total — the divergence is inside the same module.
Routine 2026-09-01 verified via direct Read of compliance.rs 262-299 — require_super_admin(&user) at :263 gates the endpoint (already tightened by PR #2907); the missing count remains.

Fix shape: add a repo count method (count_user_logs(user_id)) and use it for `total`, mirroring get_audit_logs. IG3: integration test seeding N>limit user audit logs asserts response.total == N while response.logs.len() == limit.
